chunks: One of our companions narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily Allah has created among His creatures some servants whom He has chosen for the poor among our followers, so that He may reward them for that.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It suffices for your praise of your brother when he does you a good turn that you say to him: may Allah reward you with goodness; and when he is mentioned in his absence that you say: may Allah reward him with goodness. Then you will have [adequately] recipated [his kindness].'

key_terms.أَسْدَيْتَ إِلَيْكَ مَعْرُوفًا: He did you a good turn/favor
key_terms.جَزَاءُ اللَّهِ خَيْرًا: May Allah's reward be goodness (used in absence)
key_terms.جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا: May Allah reward you with goodness
key_terms.لِفُقَرَاءِ شِيعَتِنَا: For the poor among our followers

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to say when someone does you a favor?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the spiritual merit of serving the poor within the Shia community, framing such assistance as a divinely selected role for specific servants. The Prophet’s instruction to use 'Jazāk Allāhu khayran'—both in presence and absence—emphasizes the importance of sincere, public, and private gratitude, ensuring the benefactor’s reward is secured even when he is not present to hear it.
